title: Nested Conditional Statements
learningObjectives: Explain nested conditional statements in C++ decision logic.
Identify the condition and the branch paths it controls.
Trace execution for normal, boundary and unexpected values.
Write clear and correct decision statements for a practical case.
Review common mistakes such as ordering, nesting or missing fallback handling.

understand.concept: Nested conditionals place an if or if-else inside another branch. The inner condition is checked only when its containing branch executes. Nesting should be kept shallow and readable.
understand.whyItMatters: Decision logic controls program behavior. Correct conditions, branch order, fallback paths and validation keep programs predictable and robust.
understand.explain: Use the examples to trace nested conditional statements; identify which branch is reached for each test input and explain why other branches are skipped.

practise.guidedTask: Trace all five nested conditional statements examples. For each, record the condition outcome and executed branch. Change one input to test an alternate path.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ decision-based program applying nested conditional statements to a realistic scenario. Test at least three normal cases, two boundary cases and one invalid/unexpected case.
hints: Write the condition in plain language before coding.
Trace the branch that runs for each sample value.
Keep nesting shallow and branches explicit.
Include a fallback or validation path when appropriate.

questions.prompt: When is a nested if reached?
options: When its containing outer branch executes
questions.answer: When its containing outer branch executes
questions.explanation: Inner condition is gated by outer.

questions.prompt: What is a risk of deep nesting?
Can an inner if have its own else?
questions.explanation: Nested conditions can have their own else.

questions.prompt: Which can reduce deeply nested logic?
options: Early returns or combining clear predicates
questions.answer: Early returns or combining clear predicates
